clue.text: Induced to show Kew's new variety of water-plant

indicators.note: a new variety is a fresh arrangement, so the letters of the words before it are reworked

parts.note: the setter needs only the last five letters, DUCED, of this word as fodder
Kew, the London botanic gardens, taken as written

explanation.surface: Kew Gardens is persuaded to put a newly bred pond plant on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new variety' rearranges the letters of 'Induced' and KEW, but the IN at the front of 'Induced' is surplus: the setter's fodder only works as DUCED.
explanation.definitionFit: Duckweed is the tiny floating plant that carpets the surface of ponds.

clue.text: Action (but a foreign form) of anointing

indicators.note: a foreign form of the word a is the French un, so a in the first word gives way to it

parts.note: un is the French for a

explanation.surface: A ritual act, but done in a foreign style, of anointing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but a foreign form' swaps the A of ACTION for UN, French for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction is the act of anointing with oil, as in a religious rite.

clue.text: Book Billy recommended as a certain winner

parts.note: Billy the Kid, the American outlaw, links Billy with kid
a racing tipster naps a horse he is sure will win

explanation.surface: A bookmaker named Billy tipped a horse as a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: A tipster's 'nap' is his strongest bet of the day, hence NAPPED. The book is Stevenson's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson's adventure novel of David Balfour is a classic book.

clue.text: Create havoc at the card table

definitions.note: the definition places the answer as a card game played at the table

indicators.note: to create havoc is to cause chaos, so the letters of the first word are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A player causes chaos among the cardplayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'havoc' rearranges CREATE. Ecarte is a two-handed card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecarte is a two-player card game of French origin, played at a card table.

clue.text: Where men of drive expect no confrontation

definitions.text: Where men of drive expect no confrontation

parts.words: Where men of drive expect no confrontation
parts.note: drivers on a road divided down the middle never meet oncoming traffic head-on

explanation.surface: A place where ambitious, driven people meet no opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men of drive' suggests go-getters; read it as motorists. A DUAL CARRIAGEWAY is the British term for a divided highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A divided highway separates traffic flowing in opposite directions, so motorists never face oncoming cars.

clue.text: Meadow-saffron occurs sporadically in autumn

indicators.note: happening sporadically means scattered irregularly, so the letters of the following word are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A plant called meadow saffron turns up here and there in the autumn months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporadically' rearranges OCCURS. 'in autumn' is a nod to the plant's other name, the autumn crocus.
explanation.definitionFit: Meadow saffron, Colchicum, is commonly called the autumn crocus.

clue.text: A political party 'in the money with something in the pipe-line

indicators.note: in places the article and the party inside the word for money

parts.note: cash is money
Lab is the abbreviation for the British Labour Party

explanation.surface: A political party flush with funds has a project in the pipeline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and LAB inside CASH. 'pipe-line' is the trick: a calabash is a kind of tobacco pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A calabash is a gourd, and a large curved tobacco pipe made from one, so it belongs to a line of pipes.

clue.text: Heavy smoker

parts.note: read not as a person but as a structure that sends out a lot of smoke

explanation.surface: Someone who smokes a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a chain-smoking person; the thing that smokes heavily is the flue on the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney carries smoke up from a fire and pours it out all day.

clue.text: Bird's-eye mascot for a racer?

definitions.meaning: bird's-eye is a folk name for the germander, a small blue wild flower
a racer's lucky charm would wish them speed, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is the plant called bird's-eye, and split in two it wishes a racer fast success.

clue.text: From Pan's country right away to Nova Scotia

indicators.note: away tells us the letter for right is sent off, taken out of the region's name

parts.note: Arcadia, the pastoral region of Greece, home of the god Pan

explanation.surface: A traveller journeys from the land of the god Pan straight across to Nova Scotia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes R (right) from ARCADIA. Acadia was the old French colony covering what is now Nova Scotia.
explanation.definitionFit: Acadia was the name of the French colonial territory centred on present-day Nova Scotia.

clue.text: An absolutely classic example, this case

definitions.text: An absolutely classic example, this case

parts.words: An absolutely classic example, this case
parts.note: in Latin (a classic language) grammar the case used in the construction called 'absolute' is the one named here

explanation.surface: Someone holds up a court case as the perfect textbook example.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a law case; the grammatical case is meant. The Latin 'ablative absolute' (a phrase like 'the city having been taken') gives 'absolutely' its point.
explanation.definitionFit: The ablative is the Latin grammatical case used in the absolute construction of classical prose.

clue.text: Huge old carriage with fantastic performance

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage of former times
an antic is a grotesque or fantastic caper

explanation.surface: An enormous antique coach puts on a wild show.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic means enormous, of a giant's size.

clue.text: A number of robbers said to be outlawed

indicators.note: said shows the word for a group of robbers is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a band is a group, as in a band of robbers

explanation.surface: A gang of thieves are reported to have been made outlaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Something banned is prohibited, put outside the law.

clue.text: One way to shoot birds

definitions.meaning: to fire from a hidden position
long-billed wading birds, the plural the same as the singular

explanation.definitionFit: Sniping is shooting from cover, and the snipe is a wading bird whose plural is unchanged.

clue.text: Family supports Uriah on board a wool-carrier

indicators.note: in a down entry a piece that supports another is placed below it
on, as in on board, puts the clerk inside the ship's letters

parts.note: board stands for a ship, abbreviated SS for steamship, as in going on board
Uriah Heep, the oily clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield
kin means family, one's relations

explanation.surface: Relatives prop up Uriah aboard a ship carrying wool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' puts HEEP inside SS, the ship; 'supports' sets KIN beneath it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepskin is the fleece-covered hide of a sheep, which bears its wool.

clue.text: Form of writing learner has yet to change or convert

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language, as opposed to verse
L is a learner, from the L-plates of a learner driver

indicators.note: to change says the following short word must alter its letter order

explanation.surface: A student of composition still has to switch from one style of writing to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges YET to YTE after PROSE and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A proselyte is a new adherent who has switched to a faith or cause.

clue.text: Originators of home units in Italian resettlement on the Baltic

indicators.note: resettlement moves things to new places, so the letters of the pool are rearranged
originators are what starts things, so the first letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: Italian settlers set up new homes along the Baltic coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originators of' takes H and U from 'home units'; 'resettlement' rearranges them with ITALIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithuania is one of the three Baltic states, with a coastline on the Baltic Sea.

clue.text: Nether garments of gunmen?

parts.note: a gun's rear end, where it is loaded, has the same name as old-fashioned knee trousers in the plural

explanation.surface: A question about the trousers worn by armed men.
explanation.walkthrough: Old trousers and the back parts of guns share the word; 'gunmen' are the guns' own parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeches are short trousers fastened below the knee; the breeches of guns are their rear ends.

clue.text: Naturally it provides cover for anybody

definitions.text: Naturally it provides cover for anybody

parts.words: Naturally it provides cover for anybody
parts.note: read 'anybody' as 'any body': nature supplies every body with this outer layer of skin

explanation.surface: Something that by nature offers protection to anyone at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is splitting 'anybody' into 'any body': the outer skin covers every body.
explanation.definitionFit: The epidermis is the outermost layer of skin covering an animal body.

clue.text: Symbols of power to many in the Western isles

indicators.note: in puts the numeral for many inside the island group's name

parts.note: the West Indies, the islands of the Caribbean
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: Power symbols are handed to the many on the islands to the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places C inside INDIES. In algebra an index (a power like the 2 in x squared) is a symbol of a power.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics indices are the exponents written to show a number raised to a power.

clue.text: What poachers do to southern duck

parts.note: the teal is a small freshwater duck

explanation.surface: Poachers go after a duck in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Poachers take game unlawfully, that is, they thieve.

clue.text: Like the gentleman who was a non-playing cricketer ?

definitions.text: Like the gentleman who was a non-playing cricketer ?

parts.words: Like the gentleman who was a non-playing cricketer ?
parts.note: in old English cricket the Gentlemen were unpaid players, unlike the paid Players, so non-playing means non-professional

explanation.surface: A question about a gentleman who never actually took the field at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Until 1962 English first-class cricket split Gentlemen (unpaid) from Players (paid professionals); 'non-playing' means not one of the Players, not idle.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur takes part for love rather than pay, as the Gentlemen of cricket did.

clue.text: Jinx makes Robin get two ducks

parts.note: Robin Hood, the outlaw of Sherwood Forest
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so two ducks are two Os

explanation.surface: An archer named Robin bags a pair of ducks, which brings bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of zero, written O.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodoo is a person or thing bringing bad luck, a curse.

clue.text: Lacking which, must a boatman walk ashore ?

definitions.text: Lacking which, must a boatman walk ashore ?

parts.words: Lacking which, must a boatman walk ashore ?
parts.note: a boatman without the means of propelling his canoe must wade to land, and that wading is the same word

explanation.surface: A rower wonders whether, having lost something, he must wade to the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: The word works both ways: the boatman lacks the oar-like implement, so he must wade in the shallows, which is also what the word means.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddle is a short oar for a canoe, and to paddle is also to wade in shallow water.

clue.text: Like Shakespearian theatre in the round?

definitions.text: Like Shakespearian theatre in the round?

parts.words: Like Shakespearian theatre in the round?
parts.note: Shakespeare's playhouse was the Globe, and a round shape is globe-like

explanation.surface: A question about the round staging of Shakespeare's plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre in the round' suggests staging; the point is that Shakespeare's theatre was the Globe, so anything shaped like it is globe-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Globular means shaped like a globe, that is, spherical.

clue.text: Give dramatist the boot for some trifle

parts.note: giving someone the boot means a kick
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: Someone fires a playwright over some small matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, 'Give dramatist the boot' is KICK SHAW; 'some' is a link word, and a kickshaw is a trifle or fancy delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickshaw is a dainty or trinket of little value, from French quelque chose.

clue.text: Courses to arm Smith's epicure against fate

definitions.text: Courses to arm Smith's epicure against fate

parts.words: Courses to arm Smith's epicure against fate
parts.note: Sydney Smith's gourmet verse ends 'Fate cannot harm me, I have dined today': the courses of that meal are his armour

explanation.surface: Someone named Smith seeks a way to shield a gourmet from destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue alludes to the clergyman wit Sydney Smith's recipe poem, which ends 'Fate cannot harm me, I have dined today.'
explanation.definitionFit: The main meal of several courses is what the satisfied gourmet in Smith's poem has eaten.

clue.text: Who killed Hercules ? One's suspicions include him

indicators.note: include says the words before it contain the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks who murdered Hercules and admits their suspicions take in this suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' hides the answer across 'One's suspicions'. The centaur's poisoned blood, smeared on a shirt, caused Hercules's death.
explanation.definitionFit: The centaur shot by Hercules gave Deianira his poisoned blood, which later killed the hero.

clue.text: The old army, no? Maybe part of it

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the words could be otherwise, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the old army is not perhaps a piece of the whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges ARMY and NO to OMANRY. 'it' points back to 'army': the yeomanry are a volunteer cavalry force forming part of the British army.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeomanry were volunteer cavalry regiments, later part of the Territorial Army.
